pairs.why: Both saucers are rendered almost the same way, but B's silver body and softer, calmer finish sit closer to the real cards' clean matte toy look than A's heavier, darker teal mass.
B is built like a real chunky saucer with volume and an underside, so it reads like the real toy-like objects, while A is a flat plate; B is a bit glossier, though.
B reads as a properly built astronaut helmet with a clean, softly lit white shell like the real cards, while A looks like a stylized blue-and-orange ball on a shelf.
B has believable helmet construction and the vivid pink-and-purple setting of the real cards, while A is a bare glossy white sphere on a washed-out grey shelf.
A's bright white-and-brass tube and chunky, matte toy proportions match the real binoculars and rocking chair better than B's dark, glossy navy tube.
B has the crisp, detailed cartoon scene with a richer sky and ground that the real lighthouse and motel cards show, while A looks like a sparse, flat render.
B's warm palette, glowing lit door and inviting building read like the real resort, lighthouse and motel cards, while A is cold grey and more textured.
The two drawings are almost the same in colour, shape, light and finish, so neither is meaningfully closer to the real cards.
